[[File:Revan_Malak_EGTW.jpg|thumb|250px|"Revan Mythologies" were named after the famous Jedi Revan (pictured).]]
The '''Revan Mythologies''' was a series of fables and myths recounted by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Ilia Orpin/Legends|Ilia Orpin]], who was the
[[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of a [[Jedi holocron/Legends|Jedi holocron]]. Named after the famous [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], the Mythologies provided an extensive account of Jedi history, including its [[Tho Yor Arrival|possible origins]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. Many of the Mythologies featured the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], and spoke of Jedi heroes who found Rakatan devices and were forced to choose between destroying them or being corrupted by their power. They also described countless temples and ruins on Tython, including those connected to the ancient [[Je'daii]] and to the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="NoP" />

Some [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]] considered Orpin's works to be an updated derivative reworking of the [[Qel-Droma Epics/Legends|Qel-Droma Epics]], a similar set of mythical stories that spoke of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] and the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], to better acculturate [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi younglings]] of the day.<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> On the contrary, around [[3951 BBY]], [[Jedi historian]] [[Deesra Luur Jada]] asserted that [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] had different motives for becoming [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] from Revan and [[Darth Malak|Malak]].<ref name="jvs">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>
